headline: The British leave New York for good
post_facts: The last British troops sailed away
Washington rode in to cheering crowds
New York celebrated it for over a century

scenes.text: [calmly] On this day, in seventeen eighty-three... the last British soldiers sailed out of New York City.

scenes.label: Evacuation Day, 1783
scenes.caption: Lithograph by E.P. and L. Restein
scenes.text: [thoughtfully] It was their last stronghold in the new nation.

scenes.label: years under British control
scenes.text: [calmly] They had held it for seven years.

scenes.label: Washington enters New York
scenes.caption: Print by Alphonse Bigot, 1800s
scenes.text: [warmly] Then George Washington rode in, as crowds cheered.

scenes.title: A flag on a greased pole
scenes.text: [softly] Legend says a veteran climbed a greased flagpole... to raise the Stars and Stripes.

scenes.title: Ever heard of Evacuation Day?
scenes.text: [gently] Had you ever heard of Evacuation Day?
